about: Chicago skyline from Lake Michigan looking due west. Heights in metres. architectural_m is the CTBUH 'height: architectural' (it includes spires, not antennas); tip_m is the height to the tip of an antenna. Widths (w0/w1) and setback heights are simplified drawing geometry: widths are approximate unless a building's note says otherwise, and they are not part of the height test. Coordinates are Wikipedia values given to 1 arc-second (about 30 m). Sources were read through search-result quotations, because this environment could not open skyscrapercenter.com or wikipedia.org directly.

buildings.name: Willis Tower
buildings.silhouette: Bundled tube: nine 22.9 m tubes (68.6 m square base); two tubes end at floor 50, two at 66, three at 90, two rise to the roof. Two antennas, west to 527 m, east to about 521 m.
buildings.note: Setback heights are floor counts times the average storey height (412.7 m top occupied / 108 floors = 3.82 m): floor 50 = 191 m, 66 = 252 m, 90 = 344 m. Widths seen from the east are simplified (68.6 / 68.6 / 45.7 / 22.9 m). The east antenna's height (1,710 ft, SkyscraperPage) is not from a primary source.

buildings.name: One Prudential Plaza
buildings.silhouette: Flat-topped slab with a single antenna.
buildings.note: Width approximate. Coordinates given to 4 decimals only.

buildings.name: Aon Center
buildings.silhouette: Plain square shaft with a flat top.
buildings.note: Width approximate (59 m is commonly quoted, not confirmed). Wikipedia's 362.5 m 'tip' conflicts with the flat top and is not drawn.

buildings.name: Two Prudential Plaza
buildings.silhouette: Shaft with stacked chevron setbacks to a pyramidal peak, topped by a spire (part of the architectural height).
buildings.note: Top floor about 250 m (Wikipedia mirror); the 24 m (80 ft) spire is from a single source, so the pyramid runs from 250 m to the spire base at 279.3 m. Width approximate.

buildings.name: St. Regis Chicago (Vista Tower)
buildings.silhouette: Three connected stacks of frustums of 47, 71 and 93 stories (101 floors counted in the tallest mass), lowest to the east; from the lake they stand one behind another.
buildings.note: The lower stacks' heights are stories times 362.9 m / 101 floors: 47 = 168.9 m, 71 = 255.1 m. Widths approximate.

buildings.name: Marina City (two towers)
buildings.silhouette: Two identical cylindrical 'corncob' towers with scalloped balconies. They stand east and west of each other along the river, so from the lake one hides the other: drawn as one silhouette.
buildings.note: The coordinate is the complex's. Outer diameter approximate (about 32 m is often quoted, not confirmed).

buildings.name: Trump International Hotel & Tower
buildings.silhouette: Three setbacks (at floors 16, 29 and 51, aligned with the Wrigley Building cornice, River Plaza / Marina City and 330 N. Wabash) and a spire, which is part of the architectural height.
buildings.note: Setback heights are estimates (about 61, 115 and 200 m); the roof below the spire is drawn at 340 m (sources give 340.1 m and 356 m, which differ by 4.6%). Widths approximate.

buildings.name: 875 North Michigan Avenue (John Hancock Center)
buildings.silhouette: Tapered box (top about 0.6 of the base) with twin antennas.
buildings.note: Base and top widths approximate (about 50 m to 30 m on the narrow side). The second antenna is drawn at 449.9 m (1,476 ft, SkyscraperPage citing CTBUH); which mast is shorter is not confirmed.
